# Black Pepper

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="black-pepper-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="black-pepper-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="black-pepper-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Most monitored black pepper is low in lead, cadmium and arsenic, but lead is the metal to check: the EU limit is 600 µg/kg, and several market surveys report means near or above it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in <ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Lead decides most black pepper questions; aluminium, nickel and chromium are high, but estimated spice intakes sit far below their health reference values.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Grinding and handling after harvest, the market chain, and growing origin, which alone did not predict lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Osei-Safo I, Miezah K, Sackey LNA, Adusei-Gyamf J, Abdul AM · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals">Trace and Heavy Metals in Locally and Imported Spices Sold on Markets in Accra Metropolis, Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The Scientific World Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ziyaina M, Rajab A, Alkhweldi K, Algami W, Al-Toumi O, Rasco B · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Lead and cadmium residue determination in spices available in Tripoli City markets (Libya)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">African Journal of Biochemistry Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Prefer whole pepper or controlled grinding, and ask for lot lead results with a quantification limit well below 600 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>

<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Black pepper overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Black pepper usually carries lead, cadmium and arsenic in the tens to low hundreds of µg/kg, with aluminium, nickel and chromium far higher.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cicero N, Gervasi T, Durazzo A, Lucarini M, Macrì A, Nava V, Giarratana F, Tardugno R, Vadalà R, Santini A · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs">Mineral and Microbiological Analysis of Spices and Aromatic Herbs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In WHO GEMS/Food, 362 black pepper lead results had a median of about 53–60 µg/kg, and 9 (2.5%) were definitely above 600 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Total arsenic was below detection in most of 197 results, and cadmium had a median below 7 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Lead is the metal most likely to decide a black pepper question, because a minority of lots are far higher than the rest. The EU sets a binding maximum of 0.60 mg/kg (600 µg/kg) for lead in dried fruit spices, the class that covers peppercorns as dried fruits, and Codex adopted the same 0.6 mg/kg for dried fruit and berry spices; neither sets a cadmium limit for pepper.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Market surveys outside routine monitoring report much higher lead: means of 714 µg/kg in Malaysian-grown pepper bought in Accra, 730–820 µg/kg in Libya and 2,470 µg/kg in bulk pepper from eastern Turkey.<sup class="cite">[[sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Osei-Safo I, Miezah K, Sackey LNA, Adusei-Gyamf J, Abdul AM · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals">Trace and Heavy Metals in Locally and Imported Spices Sold on Markets in Accra Metropolis, Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The Scientific World Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ziyaina M, Rajab A, Alkhweldi K, Algami W, Al-Toumi href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/mercan-yucel2022-van-spices-heavy-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mercan Yucel U · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mercan-yucel2022-van-spices-heavy-metals">Determination of Aflatoxin and For a buyer, the supported priorities are a lot-specific lead result with a quantification limit well below the applicable limit, a cadmium result for markets that set one, and a supply chain that keeps grinding and handling under control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span ## What counts as black pepper

<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one subgroup and metal; a mean and a range from the same samples are separate rows. Ratings place a reported mean, median or sample result against a pooled HMI black pepper reference built from every compatible sampling family. Same-study contrasts compare packaged with bulk pepper, retail with wholesale, or an origin with the study total. Held rows failed a check against their own paper and are shown but not compared.</p>

Dried black pepper as sold or dry weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>46.4–53 (bounded)</td><td>239</td><td>282</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>48–56.5 (bounded)</td><td>239</td><td>282</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>45 reference units; 6 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>28</td><td>17%</td></tr><tr><td>Ammar et al. 2023</td><td>1</td><td>17%</td></tr><tr><td>Cantoral et al. 2024</td><td>1</td><td>17%</td></tr><tr><td>Cicero et al. 2022</td><td>1</td><td>17%</td></tr><tr><td>Moussa et al. 2024</td><td>8</td><td>17%</td></tr><tr><td>Tinggi et al. 2025</td><td>6</td><td>17%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians from every compatible black pepper sampling family in the evidence ledger: WHO GEMS/Food region-by-year medians (black pepper, random sampling only) and per-sample or per-composite results printed by individual surveys. Each family has equal total weight; subgroups have equal weight within a family. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Black pepper is a dried spice; results reported as sold and on a dry-weight basis are pooled without moisture conversion.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1–Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>An international evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world pepper market. GEMS/Food regions are reporting regions, not growing origins. Many submissions are non-detects with differing limits, which widens the bounds. Pooling as-sold and dry-weight results without moisture conversion adds a small, unquantified basis difference. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/ammar2023-element-migration-aluminum-cookware" class="internal" data-slug="sources/ammar2023-element-migration-aluminum-cookware" data-no-cite-meta>Ammar et al. 2023</a></li><li><a href="../sources/cantoral2024-lead-levels-mexican-foods" class="internal" data-slug="sources/cantoral2024-lead-levels-mexican-foods" data-no-cite-meta>Cantoral et al. 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs" class="internal" data-slug="sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs" data-no-cite-meta>Cicero et al. 2022</a></li><li><a href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon" class="internal" data-slug="sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon" data-no-cite-meta>Moussa et al. 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland" class="internal" data-slug="sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland" data-no-cite-meta>Tinggi et al. 2025</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Table 3 prints LODs of 0.001-0.051 ug/kg, implausibly low for ICP-MS of digested solids (0.25 g diluted); the unit is probably ug/L or mg/kg. lod_ug_kg is the printed number taken at face value and should not be used to judge censoring. n=1 material; mean of three technical determinations. Total Sn.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Shared samples and study overlap</p><p>Subgroup rows, statistics of the same subgroup and the study total share samples; they are not independent results.</p><p>Each table row describes a food/analyte result. Repeated rows do not add independent samples or datasets. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach black pepper

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

Metals reach black pepper through the vine’s uptake from soil and through surfaces and equipment that contact the berries during drying and grinding.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The very high aluminium in pepper (29–540 mg/kg in Queensland retail samples) is attributed by those authors to aluminium utensils and containers in processing and to accumulation by the plant, and an Iraqi survey names drying on bare ground and wear of milling machinery as routes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Grinding and handling after import are plausible additions. In Libya, ground pepper bought at retail averaged 320 µg/kg cadmium against 150 µg/kg in wholesale lots sampled on arrival, and lead was also higher at retail (820 against 730 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ziyaina M, Rajab A, Alkhweldi K, Algami W, Al-Toumi O, Rasco B · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Lead and cadmium residue determination in spices available in Tripoli City markets (Libya)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">African Journal of Biochemistry Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Stainless steel and aluminium equipment are discussed as possible sources of chromium, nickel and aluminium, but no source measured them in pepper processing.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Deliberate lead adulteration, reported for turmeric, has not been shown for black pepper in this evidence.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ericson B, Gabelaia L, Keith J, Kashibadze T, Beraia N, Sturua L, Kazzi Z · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead">Elevated Levels of Lead (Pb) Identified in Georgian Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Annals of Global Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A Georgian household survey found one black pepper sample at 48 mg/kg lead by handheld X-ray fluorescence, but four of five were below its 4–8 mg/kg detection limit, and the paper does not say whether that sample was among those confirmed by laboratory analysis.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ericson B, Gabelaia L, Keith J, Kashibadze T, Beraia N, Sturua L, Kazzi Z · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead">Elevated Levels of Lead (Pb) Identified in Georgian Spices</a></span><span →</a></span></span></sup>



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and origins measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

For lead, the clearest comparison is form: in GEMS/Food, whole black pepper had a median of 30–52 µg/kg (28 results) against 61–68 µg/kg for ground or cracked pepper (211 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cadmium and arsenic medians in both forms sat below the reporting limits, so form does not change those comparisons.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> This is a descriptive difference across many laboratories, not a controlled grinding experiment.

Within one study, origin comparisons are more reliable. Among Queensland retail pepper, Vietnamese-grown pepper (two samples) had the lowest means of any origin for lead (60 µg/kg), cadmium (9) and arsenic (16), while Indian pepper (four samples) had the highest chromium (840) and aluminium (162,000 µg/kg) and Chinese pepper the highest arsenic (860 µg/kg, driven by one sample at 1,700).<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For chromium and aluminium, Vietnamese pepper (240 and 85,000 µg/kg) was also lower than Chinese (640 and 125,000) and Indian pepper (840 and 162,000), and single samples from Sri Lanka (50 and 39,000) and Malaysia (140 and 57,000) were lowest of all.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A single Vietnamese whole pepper bought in Saudi Arabia measured 8 µg/kg lead and 3 µg/kg cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cicero N, Gervasi T, Durazzo A, Lucarini M, Macrì A, Nava V, Giarratana F, Tardugno R, Vadalà R, Santini A · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs">Mineral and Microbiological Analysis of Spices and Aromatic Herbs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> With one to four samples per origin these are tentative patterns, not a supported preference for a country.

Retail and packaging comparisons point in different directions by metal. In Lebanon, bulk pepper had the highest cadmium (154 µg/kg against 121–136 for packaged) but the lowest arsenic (126 against 189–200), and lead was similar (284–346 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Moussa L, Hassan HF, Savvaidis IN, Karam L · →</a></span></span></sup> Ten packaged US retail products all fell in the lowest concern band of a consumer test for arsenic, cadmium and lead, while unpackaged pepper from eastern Turkey averaged 2,470 µg/kg lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gill2021-consumer-reports-spices|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gill LL, Christian TA · <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-whole-black-pepper-lower-in-metals-than-ground-pepper" data-anchor="is-whole-black-pepper-lower-in-metals-than-ground-pepper" data-question="Is whole black pepper lower in metals than ground pepper?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is whole black pepper lower in metals than ground pepper?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, yes in monitoring data: whole black pepper had a GEMS/Food median of 30–52 µg/kg against 61–68 µg/kg for ground or cracked pepper.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cadmium and arsenic medians in both forms were below reporting limits, and no single study compared whole and ground pepper from the same lots.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Processing, grinding and handling

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>

<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

No source measured a pepper processing step against a control for metals. Across 23 Iraqi spices pooled, unwashed portions carried 7% more lead and 14% more cadmium than washed portions, but no pepper-specific effect was reported.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Steam treatment, irradiation and sterilisation were not assessed for metals in any source here.

Grinding is the processing step most likely to matter.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ground pepper had a higher lead median than whole pepper in monitoring data, and one survey author avoided commercially milled spices because milling machinery can add trace elements.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants Controls for black pepper act at drying and handling, at grinding, at procurement and at the release test. The only measured comparisons are observational: retail lots in Libya carried more cadmium than wholesale lots on arrival, and a food safety management system at Lebanese packers did not lower lead or that market sets a cadmium limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European mg/kg lead, 1.0 mg/kg cadmium, 5.0 mg/kg arsenic and 0.05 mg/kg mercury.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span Record the growing origin separately from the packing country and the market where the pepper was bought, because most datasets identify only the market.<sup ## Exposure from black pepper

<a id="hmi-ing-031"></a>
<a id="how-do-inclusion-rate-processing-yield-preparation-and-other-ingredients-affect-a-finished-product-estimate"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-032"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-033"></a>
<a id="what-conclusions-require-finished-product-measurements-or-a-separate-exposure-assessment"></a>

Black pepper is eaten in small amounts, so its typical results add little to most diets.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Assuming 1.9 g of all spices and herbs a day, a Queensland study estimated that spices supplied about 0.65% of the lead reference point and 1.0% of the cadmium tolerable weekly intake for an adult, without singling out black pepper.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A consumer test classed all ten packaged US black pepper products as lowest concern at three quarters of a teaspoon a day.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gill2021-consumer-reports-spices|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gill LL, Christian TA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gill2021-consumer-reports-spices">The Trouble With Spices: Heavy Metals in 15 Herbs and Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Consumer Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gill2021-consumer-reports-spices">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

No source measured metals in a pepper-containing food together with the pepper that went into it. Seasoned foods in GEMS/Food, such as cod and peanuts with black pepper, were excluded because the pepper’s contribution cannot be separated.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Black pepper FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-black-pepper" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-black-pepper" data-question="What heavy metals are found in black pepper?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in black pepper?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Lead is the metal most often found at levels that matter; cadmium, arsenic and mercury are usually low or below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kowalska G · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">The Safety Assessment of Toxic Metals in Commonly Used Herbs, Spices, Tea, and Coffee in Poland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Black pepper also carries much more aluminium, nickel and chromium than lead or cadmium, in the hundreds to hundreds of thousands of µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cicero N, Gervasi T, Durazzo A, Lucarini M, Macrì A, Nava V, Giarratana F, Tardugno R, Vadalà R, Santini A · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs">Mineral and Microbiological Analysis of Spices and Aromatic Herbs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-black-pepper" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-black-pepper" data-question="How do heavy metals get into black pepper?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into black pepper?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Through the vine’s uptake from soil, contact with the ground during drying, and equipment during grinding and handling.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Libya, retail ground pepper had twice the cadmium of the wholesale lots it came from (320 against 150 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ziyaina M, Rajab A, Alkhweldi K, Algami W, Al-Toumi O, Rasco B · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Lead and cadmium residue determination in spices available in Tripoli City markets (Libya)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">African Journal of Biochemistry Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-organic-black-pepper-free-from-heavy-metals" data-anchor="is-organic-black-pepper-free-from-heavy-metals" data-question="Is organic black pepper free from heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is organic black pepper free from heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No. In GEMS/Food, 15 organic black pepper lead results had a median of 53 µg/kg, close to 60 µg/kg for 63 conventional results.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The organic label describes how pepper was grown, not a metal test of the lot.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-whole-or-ground-black-pepper-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-anchor="is-whole-or-ground-black-pepper-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-question="Is whole or ground black pepper lower in heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is whole or ground black pepper lower in heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Whole pepper was lower in lead in monitoring data, with a median of 30–52 µg/kg against 61–68 µg/kg for ground or cracked pepper.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Grinding is a plausible source, but no study compared whole and ground pepper from the same lot.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-countries-grow-black-pepper-with-the-lowest-heavy-metals" data-anchor="which-countries-grow-black-pepper-with-the-lowest-heavy-metals" data-question="Which countries grow black pepper with the lowest heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which countries grow black pepper with the lowest heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the one study that compared growing origins, Vietnamese pepper had the lowest lead, cadmium and arsenic, and Indian pepper the highest chromium and aluminium, from one to four samples each.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The same origin can measure very differently in different markets, as Malaysian pepper did in Australia (100 µg/kg lead) and Ghana (714 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Osei-Safo I, Miezah K, Sackey LNA, Adusei-Gyamf J, Abdul AM · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals">Trace and Heavy Metals in Locally and Imported Spices Sold on Markets in Accra Metropolis, Ghana</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The Scientific World Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oseisafo2024-ghana-spices-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-foods-seasoned-with-black-pepper-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="do-foods-seasoned-with-black-pepper-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Do foods seasoned with black pepper also contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do foods seasoned with black pepper also contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No study in the ledger measured both a pepper and the food made with it. Monitoring records for pepper-seasoned cod and peanuts exist, but their metals cannot be attributed to the pepper.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-levels-in-black-pepper-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-levels-in-black-pepper-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the levels in black pepper mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the levels in black pepper mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Because pepper is eaten in small amounts, it contributes little to most diets: a Queensland estimate for all spices and herbs together put lead at about 0.65% of the reference point for adults.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A consumer test classed all ten packaged US pepper products as lowest concern at three quarters of a teaspoon a day.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gill2021-consumer-reports-spices|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gill LL, Christian TA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gill2021-consumer-reports-spices">The Trouble With Spices: Heavy Metals in 15 Herbs and Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Consumer Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gill2021-consumer-reports-spices">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-black-pepper" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-black-pepper" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in black pepper?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in black pepper?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes for lead: the EU allows 0.60 mg/kg in dried fruit spices and Codex 0.6 mg/kg in dried fruit and berry spices, whole or ground, the classes that cover peppercorns as dried fruits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> China sets 1.5 mg/kg lead for spices, and Vietnam sets lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury limits for spices (2.0, 1.0, 5.0 and 0.05 mg/kg); the EU and Codex set no cadmium or arsenic limit for pepper.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">National Health Commission, State Administration for Market Regulation · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants">GB 2762-2025: National Food Safety Standard — Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">National Food Safety Standard of the People&#39;s Republic of China</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chinanhc2025-gb-2762-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Vietnam Ministry of Health · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT QCVN 8-2:2011/BYT</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/vietnam2011-qcvn-8-2-heavy-metals-en">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-washing-or-processing-remove-heavy-metals-from-black-pepper" data-anchor="can-washing-or-processing-remove-heavy-metals-from-black-pepper" data-question="Can washing or processing remove heavy metals from black pepper?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can washing or processing remove heavy metals from black pepper?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No study measured metal removal from black pepper itself. Across 23 Iraqi spices pooled, unwashed portions carried 7% more lead and 14% more cadmium than washed portions, consistent with part of the load sitting on the surface.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-the-arsenic-in-black-pepper-inorganic" data-anchor="is-the-arsenic-in-black-pepper-inorganic" data-question="Is the arsenic in black pepper inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is the arsenic in black pepper inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Mostly unknown: nearly all studies measured total arsenic only.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kowalska G · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">The Safety Assessment of Toxic Metals in Commonly Used Herbs, Spices, Tea, and Coffee in Poland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Eight of nine black pepper inorganic arsenic results in GEMS/Food were below detection limits of 5–18 µg/kg, and the ninth was 31 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-white-pepper-lower-in-heavy-metals-than-black-pepper" data-anchor="is-white-pepper-lower-in-heavy-metals-than-black-pepper" data-question="Is white pepper lower in heavy metals than black pepper?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is white pepper lower in heavy metals than black pepper?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The evidence here cannot say. White pepper was measured separately in the Lebanese survey and is outside this page, and the EU monitoring category mixes the two.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Moussa L, Hassan HF, Savvaidis IN, Karam L · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Impact of source, packaging and presence of food safety management system on heavy metals levels in spices and herbs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-bulk-or-loose-pepper-riskier-than-packaged-pepper" data-anchor="is-bulk-or-loose-pepper-riskier-than-packaged-pepper" data-question="Is bulk or loose pepper riskier than packaged pepper?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is bulk or loose pepper riskier than packaged pepper?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not consistently: bulk pepper in Lebanon had more cadmium but less arsenic than packaged, and similar lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Moussa L, Hassan HF, Savvaidis IN, Karam L · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Impact of source, packaging and presence of food safety management system on heavy metals levels in spices and herbs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moussa2024-spices-herbs-lebanon">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The highest lead means came from unpackaged pepper in eastern Turkey and retail ground pepper in Libya.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ziyaina M, Rajab A, Alkhweldi K, Algami W, Al-Toumi O, Rasco B · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Lead and cadmium residue determination in spices available in Tripoli City markets (Libya)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">African Journal of Biochemistry Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ziyaina2014-libya-spices-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/mercan-yucel2022-van-spices-heavy-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mercan Yucel U · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mercan-yucel2022-van-spices-heavy-metals">Determination of Aflatoxin and Heavy Metal Levels in Some Spices Sold as Unpackaged in Van Province and Health Risks Assessment of Heavy Metals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Balikesir Health Sciences Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mercan-yucel2022-van-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-common-is-black-pepper-above-the-eu-lead-limit" data-anchor="how-common-is-black-pepper-above-the-eu-lead-limit" data-question="How common is black pepper above the EU lead limit?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How common is black pepper above the EU lead limit?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In GEMS/Food, 9 of 362 black pepper lead results (2.5%) were definitely above 600 µg/kg, and 20 of 409 results (4.9%) in the mixed black and white pepper category.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-lead-added-to-black-pepper-on-purpose" data-anchor="is-lead-added-to-black-pepper-on-purpose" data-question="Is lead added to black pepper on purpose?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is lead added to black pepper on purpose?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

There is no evidence of that in the sources here. Lead chromate adulteration has been reported for turmeric, and a Georgian survey concluded that lead is likely added to some spices to enhance colour, but its single high black pepper reading was not shown to be adulteration.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ericson B, Gabelaia L, Keith J, Kashibadze T, Beraia N, Sturua L, Kazzi Z · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead">Elevated Levels of Lead (Pb) Identified in Georgian Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Annals of Global Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-is-black-pepper-so-high-in-aluminium" data-anchor="why-is-black-pepper-so-high-in-aluminium" data-question="Why is black pepper so high in aluminium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why is black pepper so high in aluminium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Aluminium in Queensland retail pepper ranged from 29 to 540 mg/kg, far above lead or cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Queensland authors attribute it to aluminium utensils and containers in processing and to accumulation by the plant, and put all spices together at about 3.4% of the tolerable weekly aluminium intake for adults.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-can-i-tell-whether-a-black-pepper-lead-test-is-good-enough" data-anchor="how-can-i-tell-whether-a-black-pepper-lead-test-is-good-enough" data-question="How can I tell whether a black pepper lead test is good enough?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How can I tell whether a black pepper lead test is good enough?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Check that the laboratory’s quantification limit is far below 600 µg/kg; ICP-MS in the surveys here reached 2–5 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kowalska G · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">The Safety Assessment of Toxic Metals in Commonly Used Herbs, Spices, Tea, and Coffee in Poland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Handheld X-ray fluorescence could not see below about 4,000 µg/kg, too high to check the limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ericson B, Gabelaia L, Keith J, Kashibadze T, Beraia N, Sturua L, Kazzi Z · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead">Elevated Levels of Lead (Pb) Identified in Georgian Spices</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Annals of Global Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ericson2020-georgian-spices-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-black-pepper-contain-mercury" data-anchor="does-black-pepper-contain-mercury" data-question="Does black pepper contain mercury?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does black pepper contain mercury?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Very little: all 26 Polish samples were below 5 µg/kg and Queensland pepper reached at most 17 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tinggi U, Farrell M, Porter J, Mitchell S, Jurd S · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Heavy metal analysis in commercial spices and herbs by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and estimated dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Exposure Assessment</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tinggi2025-spices-herbs-queensland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kowalska G · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">The Safety Assessment of Toxic Metals in Commonly Used Herbs, Spices, Tea, and Coffee in Poland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kowalska2021-metals-herbs-spices-tea-coffee-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> One Iraqi study reported 311 µg/kg, but it measured mercury after ashing at 550 °C, which drives mercury off, so that value is not used.<sup class="cite">[[sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matloob MH · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Using Stripping Voltammetry to Determine Heavy Metals in Cooking Spices Used in Iraq</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/matloob2016-iraq-spices-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
